title: Hotspot smoothing and regulated burst credits for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD for implementing a regulated burst and hotspot smoothing subsystem for Dedicated capacity. The feature introduces tenant-level burst credits, a hotspot detection signal, and smoothing policies that prevent short-term noisy-neighbor activity from causing wide degradation across tenants or violating reserved guarantees. This PRD covers policy model, config surface (API + Console), telemetry, acceptance criteria, and rollout strategy.
problem_statement: Currently short-lived activity spikes from one tenant can create localized GPU hotspotting and cause amplified queuing, KV cache churn, and kernel thrashing that degrades P99 latencies for co-located tenants. Existing reserved guarantees either allow aggressive burst exhaustion (leading to noisy neighbors) or are so strict that utilization is low. We need a middle ground that preserves reservation guarantees while allowing predictable, rate-limited bursts with graceful degradation.
goals: Reduce tenant-to-tenant latency tail impact during transient hotspot events
Provide a predictable, configurable burst model (credits + window) that can be applied per-reserved-pool
Expose simple policy knobs in API + Console and provide safe defaults for most customers
Add telemetry and alerts so SRE and customers can observe burst consumption and smoothing effects
Support canaryable rollout with config flags and opt-out for sensitive tenants
non_goals: Rewrite of the core scheduler or replacing existing kernel selection logic
Full RBAC UI for per-tenant burst tuning (targeting pool-level and tenant-tier defaults instead)
Automated billing changes tied to burst usage in this phase (billing will read telemetry but not bill directly)
user_stories: As an infra engineer, I want each reserved pool to have a burst credit ledger so short spikes can be absorbed without immediate preemption
As an SRE, I want to see hotspot score and credit utilization on the Console so I can debug tail latency incidents
As a PM, I want safe default configs so most customers don’t need to tune policies
functional_requirements: Add burst_credit_window (seconds) and burst_credit_capacity (tokens) to reserved pool config
Implement a hotspot detector that emits a hotspot_score (0-100) per node and per pool at 1s granularity
Credit deduction algorithm that consumes tokens proportional to measured request weight and hotspot_score with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping
Soft-preemption hook: when credits are exhausted, mark new incoming requests as soft-throttled with optional backoff guidance header
Configurable min_guarantee_pct that prevents soft-preemption from reducing a tenant below its guaranteed capacity
Expose API to query tenant credit status and to simulate credit consumption for testing
Console views: pool-level controls, per-pool credit dashboard, timeline of hotspot events, and recommended tuning suggestions
api_changes: Reserved pool PATCH/PUT schema extended with fields: burst_credit_window, burst_credit_capacity, min_guarantee_pct, soft_preempt_threshold, hotspot_weighting
New GET endpoint: /v1/dedicated/pools/{id}/burst-status returning current credits, recent hotspot scores, and last_soft_preempt_event
New POST endpoint for simulation: /v1/dedicated/pools/{id}/burst-simulate with synthetic load parameters (internal/admin only)
telemetry_and_metrics: Event logs include: hotpot_start, hotpot_end, credit_exhausted, soft_preempt_triggered
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests validate credit arithmetic across boundary conditions (window wrap, concurrent deduction)

Under a synthetic noisy-neighbor test (50% higher RPS from tenant A for 60s), P99 latency for unaffected tenants degrades by <= 15% compared to baseline, and P99 for the noisy tenant is bounded by the configured soft_preempt_threshold
Metrics for burst credits and hotspot score surface in Console dashboards and are queryable via the existing timeseries API
API schema changes are backward compatible: existing pool configs without new fields continue to operate with safe defaults
Feature flag gating exists so we can enable per-cluster and per-pool; rollout verifies safety during canary stage
No reserved-guarantee regressions: min_guarantee_pct honoured in failure and burst-exhaustion scenarios (automated test coverage)
success_metrics: Reduce incidents where single-tenant hotspots cause multi-tenant P99 amplifications by 60% within 30 days of rollout
Adopted by >= 40% of active dedicated pools within 12 weeks (enabled but not necessarily tuned)
Console usage: > 200 views of burst dashboard per week from oncall/ops teams in first month
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) Internal dev clusters with simulation tests (2 weeks), 2) Canary on 3 low-risk customer clusters with feature flag and manual monitoring (2 weeks), 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of dedicated capacity with automatic rollback on SLO regressions, 4) Broad enablement with safe defaults and opt-out for customers. Provide PRD + runbook to oncall and Solutions Engineering before canary.
dependencies: ENG-34521: telemetry ingestion pipeline addition for per-pool hotspot_score
ENG-36100: soft-preemption framework (hooks and headers) must be landed
DES-901: Console panel for capacity visualizations
risks: Incorrect weighting in credit deduction could unfairly throttle benign workloads
Telemetry lag could cause delayed reactions and either over-throttling or insufficient smoothing
Complexity of policy knobs may cause customers to misconfigure leading to perceived regressions
Edge cases with multi-node KV cache invalidation might still produce tail spikes despite smoothing
decisions_made: Use a token-bucket like credit ledger with decaying refill over burst_credit_window rather than a leaky-window average
Expose pool-level (not per-tenant) controls initially to reduce surface area
Soft-preemption will be preferred over hard eviction for initial release to avoid abrupt request failures
open_questions: Should credits be transferable between pools owned by the same customer? (ops+billing implications)
What is the recommended default burst_credit_window for multi-GPU pools (60s vs 120s)?
Do we surface per-tenant recommended tuning via Console AI suggestions in this phase or defer to analytics team?
